concept: The story is a contradiction: the fastest driver does not start first. So the hero is built like a split result, 'Fastest in qualifying.' in muted grey and 'Starting sixth.' in white, with the 1:33.893 lap and Verstappen's +0.258 gap as the evidence underneath. Slide 2 turns the gap into bars that grow with time lost, so Verstappen's short highlighted bar shows how close pole really was. Slide 3 explains the why with one giant number, the 5 grid places lost to new power unit parts. The last slide moves to what is still alive in a settled season: the fight for P2 between the two front-row starters. F1 red, type and data only: no driver photos, no team logos.
caption:
Fastest in Vegas. Starting sixth.

Kimi Antonelli, already the 2026 world champion, topped qualifying in Las Vegas with a 1:33.893. Max Verstappen was 0.258s slower. Yet Verstappen starts on pole.

Why: Antonelli has a five-place grid penalty for new power unit parts. GPblog reports it was his sixth ICE of the season. Oscar Piastri and Carlos Sainz also take 10-place power unit penalties.

Behind the title, there is still a race for P2 in the standings. Verstappen has 279 points to George Russell's 262. The two of them share the front row.

Can Antonelli win from sixth? Tell us below.
